title: The pilot opens and closes at a temple door
body: The first talk (Elder Gong) says temple 54 times, more than the other four talks combined (12). The last talk (President Oaks) announces that the Salt Lake Temple opens to the public on April 5, 2027, the first time since 1893. Elder Gong's own talk is a bookend too: it opens and closes on the same joke, 'Why did the temple workers cross the road?'

title: 49 scripture citations, almost nothing shared
body: Each speaker leans on a different book: President Oaks's Sunday talk is 15 of 22 Book of Mormon, Elder Gong's is 6 of 11 Doctrine and Covenants, Elder Schmeil builds on Haggai. Only two overlaps cross talks. Elder Schmeil's 3 Nephi 18:11 falls inside President Oaks's 3 Nephi 11–28, the Savior's visit to the Americas. And the closing hymn lists Doctrine and Covenants 76:41–42, inside the 76:39–43 Elder Gong cited in the first talk. The nearest miss is next-door verses: Alma 34:33 (Elder Gong) and Alma 34:32 (Elder Schmeil).

title: Covenants are the only thread through all five
body: Of the families proposed, only Covenants (43 mentions) and Faith (23) appear in every talk. Elder Schmeil alone accounts for 22 covenant mentions, and even the three-minute closing remarks end on "the covenant path". The closing hymn carries faith ("my one sure rock of faith") but never says covenant.

title: Two of the five talks are built on a President Oaks talk
body: Elder Schmeil builds his talk on President Oaks's 'Divine Helps for Mortality'. Elder Gilbert says outright that he is amplifying five principles President Oaks taught at a devotional they gave together. The prophet's earlier words are the scaffolding of other speakers' talks, not just quotes in them.

title: President Nelson is still one of the most-cited voices
body: President Nelson is cited 6 times (5 by Elder Gilbert, 1 by President Oaks), close to President Oaks's own 7. President Oaks credits 'the covenant path' to him by name, and that phrase appears in 3 of the 5 talks.

title: Elder Gilbert's is the confession talk
body: His is the only talk where 'I' outnumbers 'we' (46 to 36; Elder Schmeil is 27 to 65). He tells 6 stories, more than the other four talks together (4), and the turning point is a failure of his own: 'I may have won the debate in the moment, but I lost the Spirit.'

title: Love and truth live in one talk
body: Of 41 love words in the pilot, 28 are Elder Gilbert's; of 21 truth words, 13 are his. His title says it: Teach Truth with Love. Elder Schmeil never says love at all.

title: Faith and secular learning, from two angles
body: President Oaks names two ways of knowing, the scientific and the spiritual, and says there is no ultimate conflict between them. Elder Gilbert tells of staying quiet while academic leaders attacked faith, and a chancellor later asking his help. Doubt and fading faith is the unspoken subject both share.

title: The prophet's Sunday talk asks the most and promises the least
body: President Oaks's Sunday talk has 8 invitations and 2 promises. Elder Schmeil's is the reverse: 2 invitations and 4 promises. Across the pilot there are 22 invitations and 13 promises, and 8 invitations are paired with the promise that answers them.

title: The shared picture is a path, not water
body: Path pictures show up in 4 of 5 talks: a road, the covenant path twice, a God in relentless pursuit. The closing hymn ends on one more: "the lonely road that leads to thine eternity". Water appears only twice, as a flood of truth (President Oaks) and an anchor (Elder Gilbert). No boats yet.

title: Concrete announcements, with dates
body: 21 temples to be dedicated this year and 1 rededicated; the Salt Lake Temple open to the public April 5, 2027; a video series, Dedicate, starting right after the session. And one forward-looking statement that reads as prophecy: records of Christ's visits to other nations, including the lost tribes, will come forth.

title: The conference ends where it began: a road and a veil
body: Elder Gong opened the conference with temple workers crossing the road "to help the people on the other side", and spoke of hearts softened "on both sides of the veil". The closing hymn's last two verses sing "the light beyond the veil of death" and "the lonely road that leads to thine eternity". Even the scripture listed under the hymn, Doctrine and Covenants 76:41–42, sits inside the passage Elder Gong cited.

title: The last word is a prophet's testimony
body: President Oaks closes his remarks with his witness that truth is found in the restored gospel. Then the congregation sings words written by an earlier prophet, President Gordon B. Hinckley: "I know that my Redeemer lives". The line is Job's (Job 19:25, listed under the hymn), so the conference closes on a testimony that runs from Job through a modern prophet to the people singing it.
